 Tata Sons facing 'back-door takeover', warns Jimmy Tata

 Reeba Zachariah / TNN / Updated: Nov 17, 2026, 08:59 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Noel Tata (left) and Jimmy Tata (right) MUMBAI: Jimmy Tata, the reticent younger brother of Ratan Tata and a perpetual trustee of the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), has broken his silence after a long period to flag concerns regarding the governance of Tata Trusts and speak in favour of listing Tata Sons . Jimmy has expressed his concerns in a note regarding what he described as a potential "back-door takeover" of Tata Sons, which is majority-owned by Tata Trusts, and questioned developments that, in his view, could concentrate influence within a narrower group of trustees. Jimmy, 86, told TOI that he had recently spoken by telephone with Vijay Singh , a trustee of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT). It was this conversation that was recorded and later documented in a two-page note bearing the signatures of both. However, the oldest member of the Tata family on the board of the trusts stopped short of indicating whether he would take a more active role, saying any future action would "depend on the situation". The note argues that the induction of members of the Noel Tata family into the trusts was securing "a degree of control over Tata Sons that was never the settlers' intention. It is entirely inappropriate for more than one family member to serve on a given trust; doing so effectively confers ownership rights over the trusts' significant shareholding in Tata Sons at no consideration whatsoever." The note also criticises amendments to Tata Sons' articles of association in 2013-14, saying they "fundamentally overturned" the earlier separation between the charitable trusts and Tata Sons' commercial operations by granting the Trusts' chairman veto powers and the ability to appoint directors. The note further criticises the introduction of a "four-year time limit on the tenure of certain trustees while exempting others", arguing that it "compromised trustee independence and concentrated authority, enabling the marginalisation or removal of trustees who dissent." As an example, it cites the "targeting" of Venu Srinivasan "because he opposed the induction of Noel's son into the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, alongside the earlier removal of Vijay Singh for authoring a factual article. " It also backs the continuation of Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran, noting that he had received "overwhelming support" and delivered record earnings and dividend payouts. The note also argued that listing Tata Sons was "all the more critical" because it would "dismantle the pervasive culture of secrecy", impose greater accountability and increase scrutiny of the group's governance structure. Jimmy's status as a perpetual trustee also places him at the centre of the governance discussion. Apart from Jimmy, SRTT's perpetual trustees are Jehangir H C Jehangir and Noel. Amendments to Maharashtra's public trust law, which came into force in Sept 2025, limit perpetual trustees to one-fourth of a trust's total board strength. The provision has sparked debate over how existing appointments will be treated. Noel has maintained that the amendment operates prospectively from Sept 2025 and does not automatically affect appointments made before it came into force. Jimmy, who became a trustee of SRTT following the death of his father Naval Tata, has historically maintained a low profile in the affairs of the trust. He generally does not participate in the trust's voting process, although all resolutions and minutes of trustee meetings are routinely sent to him by post; he is not particularly tech-savvy. Asked by TOI whether he had participated in or voted at recent SRTT meetings before the public charities regulator's ban, Jimmy said he had not. On whether that position could change in the future, he replied: "It depends on the situation." Join conversation

 People familiar with the matter played down the significance of the two-page note, saying it was unclear whether it reflected Jimmy's independent views or had been prepared to advance another individual's agenda. In their view, the more consequential issue would be whether Jimmy ultimately chooses to vote on matters such as resolutions regarding Tata Sons annual general meetings or the appointment of Trusts' nominees to Tata Sons board. They also noted that presence of multiple members of the Tata family on trusts was not unprecedented, pointing out that during Ratan Tata's tenure, Ratan Tata, Jimmy and Noel were all trustees simultaneously.
